say: A house for the faithful? No. Then whose house, stranger?
Your own roof. Does the Flame know whose it is?
I'll remember this place. So will the Inquisitors.
Build what you like, outlander. Okran counts every stone.
Heresy likes quiet corners. Be sure this is not one.
We're watching you, stranger. Not unkindly.
Whose blessing did you build under? Not ours, I think.
A roof with no priest under it. That is how the rot begins.
A good house, /BROTHER/. May the Flame find it clean.
Honest work on honest ground. The Lord of Light sees it.
You build like a man with faith. Keep it.
Peace on your roof, traveller. May no darkness cross it.
Not many outlanders keep a decent house.
The faithful would sleep easy here.
Walls. Good. The Lord of Light favours a house that can be defended.
Stone against the dark. At least you have sense.
A wall is a prayer in stone. Keep it whole.
Walls keep the heretics out. Mind that they don't keep the truth out too.
Behind your walls, who do you answer to? I ask only to know.
A shack and a fire. The faithful have lived on less.
Small. Humble. The Lord of Light doesn't mind small.
One fire in the wastes. Tend it, or the dark will.
You have started. Starting is the part most don't manage.
A town, of sorts. A town needs a priest. Have you a priest?
So many roofs. Okran did not build the first Nation on less.
This is more than a camp. Holy Nation law will want to know of it.
A settlement of outlanders. I'd like to meet whoever speaks for it.
A beast with a roof. The Lord of Light weeps.
Darkness learns to build now. It won't last.
Look, it keeps a house like a man. A mockery. A dull one.
This is no house. It is a lair with a door.
Mark this place. It will need cleansing when the time comes.
Walls and doors for the darkened. What next, a church?
You hold this place? Not for long. The Flame is patient.
Heretic, your house will burn warm.
Every wall falls to the faithful. Yours is only a wall.
Build high, heretic. It is farther to fall.
The Lord of Light sees this place.
You made a home in sinful ground. I'll help you leave it.
Blessings upon this house, /BROTHER/. Is there bread?
May the Lord of Light keep your walls and your sleep.
Your doors are open to the faithful.
A holy house, however small. Well done.
A town worthy of the Nation. Okran would nod, I think.
The Holy Nation could use a settlement like this on the road.
You have built where others only passed.
Should the Nation need a hall in these lands, we know whose door to knock.
A fine house for a heretic. The Flame will leave it standing, perhaps.
You build well. It makes the sin worse.
A handsome place. Pity who lives in it.
Fine stonework. Heretics always take pride in their cages.
That is a good house. The faithful would be glad of it.
A tidy place. Keep it free of darkness.
Well made. Whoever built this had faith in his hands at least.
I've seen worse chapels. This is better than most.
Blessed craftsmanship, /BROTHER/. The Lord of Light favours the builder.
A true house of the faithful. I will tell the others.
You've done well here. The Nation sees it.
Now that is a house worth defending.
The land is returned to the Lord of Light.
Purge it. Burn what will not be blessed.
Cleansed. Another stone in the Nation.
Heretics out. The faithful in.
Hold the gate. Let none of the darkness back in.
This ground was always ours.
A /FLATSKIN/ builds. Does he know what he builds on?
Your wall faces the wrong way. A Shek child would see it.
You hold ground. Can you hold it when warriors come?
Poor ground. Good ground is won, not bought.
A fortress is a promise to fight. See that you keep it.
I judge your defences, /FLATSKIN/. They aren't kind to you.
You build as warriors build. Plain and strong.
A solid place, /FLATSKIN/. Better than I expected.
This house has been thought about. Good.
There's honour in a well-held home.
Good walls. A warrior's house. I approve, /FLATSKIN/.
Walls tell me you expect a fight.
Stone is honest. It doesn't lie about what it will stop.
Strong walls. Now, who stands on them?
Your gate is your pride. Keep it shut to cowards.
A whole settlement. A /FLATSKIN/ doesn't often finish what he starts.
You have raised a town in the dust.
So many roofs to defend. Do you have so many spears?
The Kingdom may wish to know who rules this place.
A hall for a Shek in foreign land. Kral sees it, kinsman.
You raise a house for our people.
Shek build, Shek hold. Well met, kinsman.
This ground is yours by blade and by work.
Your walls are paper. I have broken thicker.
You made a home, /FLATSKIN/. Now you have more to lose.
I will take this house and sit in your chair.
A fine hall. It would look better with a Shek flag.
Hold your gate, if you can. I would enjoy it.
Your hall is well kept, friend.
I would fight beside you on these walls.
There is honour in this house. I feel it.
Shek do not praise lightly. This is a good place.
A good building. There's skill in it.
Well made. The Stone Golem would approve.
Solid and plain. Just so.
I have seen Shek halls less sound than this.
A hall worthy of a warrior. I'll speak of it.
You honour us by building well, friend.
This is how a home should look.
Kral smiles on a house like this.
This ground is Shek now. Kral watches.
Throw the flatskins out. Keep the walls.
Raise the banner. Let them see who holds this.
A good hall. We'll make better use of it.
Your own place, eh? Registered? No? Hm.
Building on Empire land with no paperwork.
Somebody's going to want a cut of this. Might as well be us.
Pretty. Pay your dues and nobody has to ask about it.
Under whose charter, stranger? I ask only so I can write it down.
The Empire keeps ledgers on everything, even this.
Nice outpost. A civilised corner of the wastes.
Law and order, one wall at a time.
You have the look of a proper tax-paying citizen.
A tidy house on a tidy road. The Empire could use more.
Walls, a gate, a lock. Good. Crime will have a harder time.
Fine walls. Mind who you lock out, and who you lock in.
A walled hold. That counts as a town in some books.
Behind walls and no permit. That's a fine trick.
A hut and a fence. Not taxable.
Small. Too small to bother with. Come back when you are bigger.
A shack is a shack. Grow, and the Empire will find you.
Cosy. The tax collectors will not find it. Cosy.
This is no camp, this is a town. Towns pay tithes in the Empire.
So many roofs! An assessor would weep for joy.
A settlement of this size draws the eye of every lord on the road.
You have built a town. Expect visitors with ledgers.
Skeletons and Shek and worse, setting up house on Empire sand.
A strange sort of landlord, this. Does the Empire know?
They're settling in? On Empire ground? The Lords will love that.
Not a face I'd have picked for a neighbour. Business is business.
Nice walls. You won't need them once the Empire gets hold of you.
Your place will make a fine garrison. Thank you for building it.
I know your face. The ledger knows your name.
That's Empire land you're sitting on.
A friend in the outlands. Always good to know a landlord.
Your place keeps the road safer. The Empire thanks you.
If there's a bed going, I'll pay in cats.
A strong outpost makes a strong ally. I'd say the same to the Lords.
Pretty place for a criminal.
An excellent building. The tax collector will have a field day.
Well built, I'll say that. Which makes it worth confiscating.
I admire your workmanship. I'll appraise it later.
A fine building. Whose permit is it under?
Handsome work. Properly built, properly drained.
Well made. That sort of thing raises the value of the road.
Good lines, solid roof. The City would approve, if it noticed.
A credit to the district. I'll mention it in my report.
That's how a proper outpost should look.
Splendid. I'd vouch for it at any gate in the Empire.
You have a talent for this. The Empire could use you.
Stop right there. This place is against Empire law.
Whatever is going on in there, it's finished. Hands where I can see them.
An illegal operation, and you're the owner.
Don't trouble yourself to explain. The law has already read this building.
You there. That building isn't permitted under Empire law.
I've seen what's in there. Shut it down or I will.
Some things you can't do on UC land. This is one of them.
That's no honest trade. Close it. Do it now.
A warning, then, since I am in a good mood. Close it.
Friend, I don't want to write this. That building is illegal here.
I like you. That's why I'm telling you to shut it down.
Whatever is in there, I didn't see it.
Get rid of it before somebody less friendly walks by.
Setting up shop on guild roads? Fees apply, you know.
A little outpost, no permit. The Guild regulates all trade out here.
Your prices had better match ours, or the Guild will notice.
I see a shop in the making. I see a fee in the making.
A fine place for a market. Roads this way want one.
Good location. Traffic, good water, and a wall. That's a trade post.
If you stock proper goods, the Guild could do business here.
Not bad at all. You could turn a profit here.
Walls mean safe stock. Safe stock means better prices.
A walled place. Merchants like that.
Walls and a gate. Now if only you had a counter.
A wall around the stock is worth more than a lock on the door.
I smell trade. Do you sell here? Do you buy?
If you keep a shop, I'll take a look.
A new place on the road. I'll see what the shelves hold.
Prices are what matter. Where do you stand on prices?
Nobody else sells here, I take it. Good. Nobody to undercut.
I knew a guild permit would be too much to ask.
You built this? Pity. The Guild will price you out of it.
I hope you like empty shelves.
The Guild has long arms. Your place is in reach.
Friend of the Guild, friend of mine. Let us talk prices.
Good to see you. Is the shop open? I have goods.
The Guild will hear that you run a decent place.
You and I could make good money, with a road between us.
Nice place. Good for a trade post.
A building like that raises the value of the whole road.
Well put together. Do you rent?
Solid. I'd store goods there.
That's a real trade house. The Guild would back it.
Good stonework, good road, good friends.
You have the makings of a market town. I mean it.
A place like that makes a trader feel safe.
Founded a little outpost without a permit, I see. The Guild would like a word.
No permit on this ground. Do you plan to trade, or only to sit?
Trade on the Guild roads is by permit. Raise this with me, not with the gate guards.
A man who builds first and asks later.
Your own place. Does it buy or sell? Either is fine.
No Guild, no tax, no fee? That is how I like it.
Out here by yourself. Good for you. Hard for you.
I wouldn't mind a roof for a night. Are you charging?
Good place. A free post, no fees.
A man who builds his own market. I salute him.
You have a good spot here.
This is how every town in the Empire started. A man, a wall, a fire.
Walls make me feel safe about my cart. Nice.
I'd leave my goods behind a wall like that.
A gate that shuts. That's a good thing for a trader.
A wall and a gate. That's the price of a quiet night.
I have goods and a long road. What do you stock?
If you buy, I sell. Simple as that.
No Guild tax here, I take it. That already beats most places.
I'll look around. I hope you have more than rope and lice.
Any dealer here with decent prices? Point me.
Friend, I have a few things for sale if you want first look.
A free house on a free road. Cheers.
You always know where the good stuff is.
I'll tell others to stop here.
Nice little place. Shame the road runs through it.
I have no quarrel with a building.
Free trade, no Guild. Free to be robbed, too.
I'll remember you. Prices will reflect it.
Now that's a fine building. Whoever put that up was no fool.
Good lines. A trader could rest behind that.
I'd stable a cart there, no question.
Neat. A proper place, not just a shack.
That is a building I would trust with my goods.
Good building, good friends. Hard to beat.
I'll put in a good word for this place on the road.
Strong work. People pass this way and will stop.
Whose house is this? And does it hold anyone who didn't choose to be here?
I look at every new building the same way. Where are the doors, and who holds the keys?
You built here. Good. Remember what you build it for.
Hmm. I'll be watching what comes out of that gate.
A place like this gives people a reason to stop running.
Good. A house where nobody is chained.
Safe walls, free people. That's all anyone wants.
You have done something decent. It is rarer than you think.
Walls to keep people out. See that they never keep people in.
A gate that opens both ways.
Walls are fine. A cage behind them isn't.
Keep the gate open to anyone running. That's my only ask.
Friend, there are runaways on the road. Is there room?
This is a refuge, whether you named it or not.
Your walls have saved lives. I've seen it.
The cause is lucky to have a house like this near the roads.
A whole town of free people. That's worth more than a victory.
Enough people here to be a threat to slavers.
You have built something the slavers will hate.
If slavers come, this place won't stand alone.
It's a good house. May nobody in it ever be sold.
A fine, decent place. Hold to what it stands for.
Well made. Someone cared about this.
I like this place. I don't say that often.
A true place of freedom. I'll tell the others where it is.
This is what we fight for. A house, a wall, a fire, and nobody owned.
Your house is a banner for us.
I'd lay my head down there happily.
You made a house on slave money, did you? I hope it chokes you.
Whatever you did to build this, we saw. We remember.
A pretty place built on someone's bad day.
You own people? Then this is a prison to me.
Good ground. Wide yard. I could fit forty cages in that.
Nice place. Plenty of room for a pen.
A man with a house has goods worth taking. Do you have goods?
I look at that wall and I see a buyer's gate.
Solid walls. That keeps the stock in and the thieves out.
I wouldn't mind a wall like that around my yard.
Walls like that would hold a hundred.
Good wall. A man could keep a lot behind it, if he wanted.
So many people living in one place. Do they know their value?
A settlement. Free people, mostly. That's a lot of potential stock.
Lots of hands here. Hands are cats, in the right market.
Count the heads. Think about the money. That's all I do.
Good place for a pickup. We pay well on delivery.
I might do business here, if you do.
Take a seat. Tell me what you have. I tell you what it's worth.
Hm. You keep a tidy place.
I will take this place. Then I will sell everyone in it.
Your walls will make a fine pen.
Count heads. I want a number before we start.
What a beautiful stockyard you built for me.
A friend of the trade. Care to sell?
Good place. Let us talk about the business.
I could use a base on this stretch. Do you rent?
You and I could make cats here.
A pretty building. Someone with taste. Someone who pays.
I'd put an auction block in front of that.
A fine place to watch a sale from.
Good lines. I could fill it.
Round them up. Everyone. Leave nobody running.
This place is ours. The people in it too.
Lock the gate. Count them. Price them.
A fine hold. We'll put it to use.
Your own place. Runaways like such places. I'll keep an eye out.
A house where nobody asks questions. That's where runaways go.
If you shelter any of my quarry, you'll hear from me.
I smell a base for runaways. Don't make me prove it.
No-hive builds. Strange. What for?
A home with no queen. How does it hold together?
This one builds alone. Odd.
The drones do not build alone. Why does he?
A good nest. Hive would be glad of it.
You build like a hive builds. Many hands.
Safe walls, many workers. The Queen would nod.
This is a good place to work. I could stay.
Many hands live here. Many hands build.
The drones count. They count many here.
A great nest, for no-hive. Strange. Good.
All of these work together? Even without a queen?
Walls. Good. Walls are a hive.
Walls keep the nest warm. Keep them.
A shell of stone. The Queen would like that.
Stone shell. Many workers inside. Good.
A Prince keeps a house of his own. That's a rare sight.
One of us, building. The Queen's thoughts are far away, but I like it.
A Prince with walls of his own. It is good.
Our people build in the wastes now. That is proper.
A worker like us, building. Good.
One of us, with a house. Yes.
You build. I carry. We are the same.
Drones count. You count too.
No-hive nest. Death to it.
The walls will not stop us.
A no-hive builds. The drones will break it.
Burn the nest of the no-hive.
A friend of the Hive builds well. Good.
The Hive is glad. The drones are glad.
Many hands will visit your nest.
A good place. We'll carry the word.
A good nest. Strong and clean.
The drones would build it the same.
A fine place. We would live in it.
Good work. The workers admire it.
The Hive will remember this place.
A true friend's nest. We'll protect it.
A house the Queen would admire, I think.
Good. Good. Come, tell us how it's made.
Greeeee! The nest is ours!
The no-hive are out. The drones come in.
Break the doors. Carry the nest away.
Greeeee! Drones, take the walls!
They live inside stone. We live inside a hive.
They have built so many roofs. We would need a queen for all of them.
I don't understand why no-hives need so many walls.
All of these roofs. Who tells them what to do?
Structure detected. Purpose unknown.
Walls, roof, door. Adequate. Inefficient.
Why does a human sleep under so many things?
Observation. This place. Efficiency estimated at sixty percent.
Efficient. I note the angles. Good.
A sound structure. Not wasteful.
This works. I will not say it twice.
Good enough. A skeleton could live here.
The walls are adequate. The gate is the weak point.
Perimeter noted. It leaks, a little.
Walls are a sensible use of stone. Continue.
Wall thickness is sufficient for the current threat level.
Many structures. Many occupants. Assessing. Not an efficient system.
This settlement has too many doors.
Large population. Resource burn estimated high.
So much housing. Skeletons do not need it.
A skeleton builds? Good. Few do.
A builder like me. Working structure. Good.
Same as me. We build without being asked.
One of us, with a roof. Why does one of us need a roof?
The structure is a target.
Walls are an obstacle. Obstacles are removed.
Your structure won't hold. I have tested better.
I compute three weak points. Four.
Your structure is acceptable. I will use it.
A good place to wait. I'll remain.
A safe base. Keep it that way.
Efficient. I like efficient.
Good structure. Efficient.
A sound build. I approve.
Square corners. A pleasing result.
Well built. Few humans build well.
Efficiency high. Structure sound. Approved.
I would not change a single plank.
This place works. That's rare.
I'll remember where this is.
Feeble humans. Out.
The structure is claimed.
Humans leave. Skeletons stay.
The place is ours. The humans aren't.
/CANNIBALTASTY/ walls. We climb. We eat in your house.
Nice house. Nice big pot. /CANNIBALHA/!
Many people in house. Many meal in house.
Walls no stop hunger. Walls only slow.
/CANNIBALHA/! New place to eat!
Your house our house. Your pot our pot.
/CANNIBALKA/! Good, soft house.
Everybody who stay get cooked. Everybody.
House of meat. Many soft ones, I dhink.
You build good pen. We come back.
So tidy. Good place to hide from. Good place to come back.
Walls look strong. Strong walls make people feel safe. /CANNIBALTASTY/.
Pretty house. Pretty meat inside.
We watch from grass. We watch long time.
So many light. So many sleeper. /CANNIBALHA/.
Strong house. Nice soft inside, yes?
What a lovely lodging. I do so enjoy a home with good light for sewing.
A well-kept house. A well-kept man.
I do hope your walls aren't too thick. They're so hard to stitch.
Forgive the intrusion. I like to see where a man keeps his skin before I borrow it.
How charming. Do come out, one at a time. I'll measure you at the door.
This will do very nicely. I'll take the large room.
Everyone out of the house. Gently. You'll bruise.
Lovely place. I'll need to rearrange the furniture.
What a fine house. May I come in? Only to look at the people.
I notice a great deal of lovely skin on the premises.
Pretty place. Do you sleep with the door locked? Please do.
A house is only as good as its occupants. May I meet them?
That's a house with real skin in it.
I like how they hold the doors open. Almost an invitation.
It would suit a collection beautifully.
Such delicate craftsmanship. Almost as good as mine.
Walls. Light. It will not hold.
You built in the fog? We breathe the fog.
Stone does not stop the fog. Stone only keeps you inside it.
We watch the lights in your windows.
A house in the grey. It will not last.
Candle in the fog. Easy to find.
A pretty fire. We will come to see it.
You make noise, you make light.
That is a fine house. It will make a fine pyre.
We saw your wall. We heard your gate.
So many sleepers. So close to the fog.
We watch your doors. We always watch.
The fog is in your house now.
Keep still. The grey will pass you.
Take the walls. Leave the dead.
No more lights. Only the fog.
Nice place. Anyone home who's worth a look?
Pretty walls. What's behind them? Loot?
I count a few doors, a few barrels, a few throats.
Got walls, got a gate, got a bed. Gotta get something worth taking.
That's your house, is it? Perfect. I'll be sleeping there tonight.
Walls ain't gonna help you. Gate ain't gonna help you.
Look at all that stuff! I want it.
You built it. We'll live in it.
Boot 'em out! Throw their stuff in the dust!
Ours now! Nobody touches the beds but me.
/LAUGH/! Pass me a drink!
We're gonna live here and eat all your food.
Nice house. Nice enough to burn.
That would make a good hideout.
I want it. Lemme see the lock.
What a place. Must be full of good things.
Good walls. They got something worth hiding.
Gate's thin. I could kick it in.
I could climb that wall by dinnertime.
Walls and a gate. They never stopped me before.
Good place, friend. Ever need a hand getting what's not yours, say so.
Heh. A decent bar, a good roof, a locked door. Got any spare beds?
Keep this place standing and I'll keep the others off it.
You got food in there? A man gets hungry.
So much house. So much food in it?
Spare a crust, house-man?
I see a roof. I see a pot on the fire. I'm hungry.
Behind those walls, someone is eating.
Give us the food. We will not touch the walls.
We'll eat your house. Door by door.
You hoard. You build walls to hoard.
We're hungry. Walls aren't.
Food! Find the food!
Eat. Eat. Eat everything.
There's bread! Get the bread!
No more starving. No more! Feed us!
A house with a full pot.
Look at those walls. Walls mean food.
A rich man built that. A rich man eats.
I'd kill for a bowl in a house like that.
Somebody built a fort out here. Brave. Stupid.
Look at that place. Who lives there? What's inside?
A house this far out has to be hiding something.
I'll be keeping this place in mind for next season.
Pretty walls. I'll take them down with you in them.
Hold the gate if you want.
Your little fort will make a nice bonfire.
All this work. All for us.
Take it! All of it!
Out! Out! Out of our house!
We could stay here. Eat. Sleep.
Good loot. Better house.
Nice little outpost. It would be a shame if it came to harm.
Somebody ought to look after a place like that. For a fee.
I see walls. Walls need protection. That costs.
A home without a friend is a home waiting to burn.
A base of your own. Hope you can afford a guard for it.
Nice place. Who's guarding it? Nobody? I don't do that kind of favour.
Everybody builds a place sooner or later. Nobody can hold it for long.
You build, I fight. That's how the world works.
Solid place. Does it have a job board? I need work.
If you need blades for hire, I know a few.
A man with walls has enemies. A man with enemies needs help.
Nice fort. I could stay a night, for a rate.
Walls are only as good as the swords behind them.
Decent walls. Who stands on them? That's the question.
Good defences, mostly. I'd reinforce the gate.
I have broken walls like these.
That's a lot of people to defend. Must pay well to hire for.
A town. You'll need a guard.
Big place. Big ambitions. Big enemies.
With a place like this, you must be hiring.
Nice walls. I've been paid to knock down worse.
I don't hate you. I'm just paid to.
You built it, I break it.
Whoever paid me knew what he was doing. This is a good target.
Friend, if you need blades, I'm your man.
Good fort. I'd stand a watch here for a fair price.
I've seen a lot of bases. This one is better than most.
You keep a clean fort. It tells me who to fight for.
A good piece of work. Whoever built that knew their craft.
Tidy. I like a base that makes a guard's job easy.
A good bed for a mercenary.
Neat, solid, defensible. What more is there?
We were paid for this. Now we hold it.
Secure the gate. Count the loot.
Nice base. Now it's ours.
Your walls, our wage.
A fixed address. Handy. Anyone with a bounty on his head should avoid one.
A man with a base is a man who can be found.
Your gates are not locked to me, I think. A man with a house has a name.
Hm. I'll remember this place, in case I need to find someone.
A real roof. Huh. Been a while.
Your own place? Must be nice.
Do you let people in? No? Fair enough.
I wouldn't mind a wall at night.
That looks warm. You hiring?
Place like that could use a hand.
Is there room? I don't need much.
Good place. Quiet. Safe. I'd take it.
Walls. A gate. Real food, I bet.
A wall that actually keeps the dark out. I envy you.
Nice and safe in there. I can feel it.
I'd sleep outside your wall and be glad of it.
Any work here, friend? Any bread?
You keep a good house. People like us talk about it.
If you ever need a body for the walls, I'm one.
I'll tell the other roamers your door is open.
That's a house. A proper house. I forgot what they look like.
A roof like that and I'd never leave.
I'd give an arm for a hearth like that.
Whoever built that's a lucky man.
Thank you for building a place a body can feel safe near.
Your house gives a body hope.
A good house. Good people in it, I hope.
I walk past it and feel the weight lift.
Is there room for another pair of hands? Not asking for much.
I can carry, I can chop. Take me in?
I'd work for a bed.
Any chance of a place here? I have nowhere else.
A wall. We prefer wind. But yes, a wall is a wall.
You stay in one place. Strange.
A house is a heavy thing.
Your fort won't move. The land does.
A good place to rest for a night.
Nice. A nice place to share a fire.
The wind blows around you. That's a good sign.
We pass this place often. It looks the same each time. That's good.
Strong place. It will last. We won't.
A fine house for a fixed man.
It's well made. We wouldn't live in it.
Good. The road needs a few places that stay.
Friend of the road, your fire is welcome.
We'll trade for a night under your roof.
Your house is a good place. The herd likes it.
We sell and we buy. Do you do both?
We carry what we carry. Do you buy?
A fixed place needs goods from outside.
My cart is full. Your shelves aren't.
Name what you need. We find it.
